title: invariant
description: A rule that must hold everywhere, stated once, and the checker holds every document to it. An invariant is a rule of the business, so it lives in a feature's domain/. It comes in exactly one of two forms. `access`: domain port operations, and what must gate every way in that reaches them -- the invariant says the gate stands, the policy behind it says what it decides. `holds`: a core shape, and a rule over its fields in the grammar a switch rule uses -- the checker proves it where it can and the compiler guards the rest.

$schema.description: The kind of this document: its published schema URL, or the alias @wilanis/invariant.schema.json.

description.description: What this invariant asserts, and why it is a rule rather than a habit, in one or two sentences.

label.description: A short human name for this document, shown wherever a reader sees it instead of its path. Absent: the file name stands in.

access.description: The access form: domain port operations, and what must gate every trigger that reaches them. Reaching is transitive, so a domain graph cannot route around the invariant by calling the operation itself. It never names a role: a role is what a policy's graph decides.

over.description: The domain port operations this invariant gates, as path#operation. A native port or an operation of one is refused (I002).

requires.description: What every trigger reaching those operations must attach: a named policy, what some attached policy must prove, or both.

policy.description: The policy every reaching trigger attaches, by path. Attached bare or with credentials, either satisfies it.

proves.description: request.* paths some policy the trigger attaches must prove, by its own `proves` (the path itself or one above it). Names what must be established rather than which policy establishes it, so signed-in, employees-only and can-record all qualify and a public trigger does not.

holds.description: The field form: a core shape, and a rule its values always satisfy. Where a value of the shape comes into being, the rule is proved from the documents or guarded by a switch the compiler lowers.

on.description: The core shape this rule is about, by path. An edge shape or a document that is not a shape is refused (I002): the edge is judged by the trigger.

when.description: The rule, in the grammar a switch rule uses -- has(), len(), comparisons, in, &&, ||, ! -- whose roots are the shape's fields: "len(url) > 0 && (method != 'DELETE' || has(ua))".

oneOf.description: The access form: `access`, and no `holds` beside it.
The field form: `holds`, and no `access` beside it.
